headline: 4.28kg of kush seized: Indian national arrested at Dhaka airport
summary: The Department of Narcotics Control arrested a 40-year-old man from West Bengal who had concealed the cannabis-based drug under sarees in his luggage.
details: The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) arrested a 40-year-old Indian national, Abhijit Das, with 4.28kg of kush, a cannabis-based drug, at Dhaka’s Shahjalal International Airport on Wednesday afternoon.
Das, a railway porter from North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, was detained at the Green Channel after arriving on a Thai Airways flight from Bangkok.
A search of his trolley bag revealed the drugs concealed beneath three Indian sarees. Officials also seized his passport, a smartphone, and foreign currency.
According to the DNC, an international drug trafficking ring operates across three countries, recruiting low-income Indians from Kolkata to smuggle drugs into Bangladesh via Bangkok.
The syndicate is allegedly attempting to create a new market for kush in Bangladesh, using 'visa-free' travel facilities to transport the contraband.
Das had reportedly planned to stay in Bangladesh for a few days to hand over the consignment before returning to India through the Benapole land port.
A case has been filed under the Narcotics Control Act at Airport Police Station. This follows another arrest of an Indian national with 3kg of kush at the same airport on August 22.

headline_marked: Two babies [[stolen from Cox's Bazar hospital]] in 20 days
headline: Two babies stolen from Cox's Bazar hospital in 20 days
summary: Serious security lapses at Cox's Bazar District Sadar Hospital are under scrutiny after two infants disappeared from different wards within three weeks.
details: Two infants have been stolen from Cox's Bazar District Sadar Hospital within 20 days. The first child vanished from the children's ward on September 19, while a newborn disappeared from the Special Care Newborn Unit (SCANU) on October 9.

On September 19, an unidentified woman approached a mother in the children's ward, offered to comfort a seven-month-old baby named Rakib, and walked out with him. CCTV footage showed the woman leaving in an autorickshaw with two young girls.

On October 9, a woman wearing a burqa and face mask allegedly entered the SCANU step-down ward and took a newborn. The mother, Rozina Akter, realized the child was missing around 2:30 am, after which she alleged that a doctor initially told her not to inform her family.
Police and a hospital inquiry committee are investigating the cases. Sub-Inspector Rajib Pal noted that most of the hospital's CCTV cameras are out of order, hindering the identification of suspects.
Hospital authorities claim they have requested additional police protection, while police point to internal security shortcomings. Neither child has been found, and no arrests have been made so far.
